purpose: Acquisition candidates and decided exclusions. NOT the ingestion source of truth — that is ingest/sources.config.json, and nothing here is ingested until it is promoted into that file with full provenance. Kept separate because candidates, blocked works and exclusions have different required fields than acquired works, and forcing them into the sources schema would make the fail-closed licensing guards grow status branches.
rules: docs/pm/CORPUS_CEILING_2026-09-07.md §Universal rules binds every entry here: per-work provenance record, the edition trap, CCEL markup restriction, SWORD .conf check, forbidden hosts, the name-collision trap, ADR-029 composite-volume slicing, adapter-readiness, the 95-year/URAA term rules.

blocked_on_values.archive-adapter: archive.org OCR only; src/ingest/adapter-archive.ts has one profile (thayers-lexicon). Needs a profile before this can be promoted.
blocked_on_values.null: Acquirable today through an existing adapter (gutenberg | ccel | sword) or a structured source.

exclusions.title: Word Studies in the Greek New Testament

exclusions.title: A Greek-English Lexicon (LSJ, 9th edition)

exclusions.title: Douay-Rheims Bible (Challoner revision)
exclusions.author: Richard Challoner (rev.)
exclusions.excluded_reason: OWNER RULING 2026-09-07: declined. Not a licensing or availability question — the text is PD and was researched as the single highest-value translation acquisition. Recorded so it is not re-proposed.

judgment_calls.title: The History of the Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire
judgment_calls.author: Edward Gibbon
judgment_calls.question: In scope? Immensely well-known and PD (1776-89, Gutenberg/archive.org), but it is a secular political history of the whole Roman Empire — only ch. 15-16 and scattered later material is church-relevant. Ingesting whole would be mostly off-register; a selective slice cuts against the corpus's no-excerpt discipline.

judgment_calls.title: History of the Church Missionary Society
judgment_calls.author: Eugene Stock
judgment_calls.question: In scope? The historian register is scoped as 'biblical/Jewish background + church history'. Missions history is adjacent, not clearly inside it. Needs a deliberate scope decision, not a default yes. 1899, 4 vols, archive.org.
